title: Revenue tile shows shop supplies as an Other share
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  • You are in location {Location-A}, where nothing else is invoiced, credited or clocked this week. On the Dashboard, the Revenue tile on This Week reads $0.00 with "0 Invoices".
    For example: {Location-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C614718 Other Shop.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has one asset, {Unit-A}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C614718 Other Fleet and {Unit-A} is ZZ-C614718-1.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} and {Unit-A} is reviewed and not invoiced. It has one approved labor line, {Line-1}, of 3.00 hours at $100.00 an hour, one part, {Part-A}, with Sell Price $100.00, and shop supplies of 10% of labor.
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-15500, {Line-1} is ZZAUTOTEST C614718 Line 1 and {Part-A} is ZZAUTOTEST-C614718-P1.
  • Starting screen: the Dashboard at {Location-A}.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click Work Orders in the top menu and open {Work-order-1}.
  2. Click the Finance tab and click Create Invoice.
  3. Close the New Customer Payment dialog without paying.
  4. On the invoice, read the Labor, Parts, Shop Supplies and Subtotal amounts.
  5. Click Dashboard in the top menu and set the Revenue tile's date range to This Week.
  6. Read the Revenue headline.
  7. Read the line under the Revenue headline.
  8. Click the report arrow beside the Revenue tile's name.
  9. In the Sales report, read the Labor column figure for this range.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Work-order-1} opens.
  • Step 2: The invoice is created and the New Customer Payment dialog opens.
  • Step 3: The dialog closes and the invoice stays unpaid.
  • Step 4: The invoice shows Labor $300.00, Parts $100.00, Shop Supplies $30.00 and Subtotal $430.00 (for example). Write the four amounts down.
  • Step 5: The Revenue tile shows This Week.
  • Step 6: Revenue reads the invoice Subtotal, to the cent (for example $430.00).
  • Step 7: The line reads "Parts 23% · Labor 70% · Other 7%" (for example). Parts = 100 ÷ 430 = 23.3%, so 23. Labor = 300 ÷ 430 = 69.8%, so 70. Other = the shop supplies, 30 ÷ 430 = 7.0%, so 7. Each is a whole number, the three add up to 100, and the shop supplies are not counted in Labor.
  • Step 8: The Sales report opens on the same dates (This Week).
  • Step 9: The Labor column shows the invoice's labor only (for example $300.00), the same labor figure the tile's Labor share is worked out from.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9576 (Story 4, KPI Hero Tiles), story SV-9575 (Story 3, Measure Formulas), story SV-9582 (Story 10, Report Drill-In); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v50 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 16 Oct 2026, S4-R3 (reworded in v50 after Ayesha Khan's question of 16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward's ruling in the PRD Change Log), S3-R2 table (Revenue row), S10-R1. Source-verified 16 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R2 table: Revenue: “Revenue | Sum of invoice subtotals in the selected range, before any discount and before tax, minus credit memos. Shown to the cent. | Sales report”
  • S4-R3: “The Revenue tile shows a supporting line reading "Parts {parts}% · Labor {labor}% · Other {other}%", each percent a whole number of the tile’s revenue. Parts is parts sales, net of credits (as today). Labor is labor sales only, the same figure as the Sales report’s Labor column. Other is everything else in revenue: shop supplies, fees and any other line that is neither a part nor labor. The three are rounded so they always add up to 100. "· Other {other}%" is left off when Other rounds to 0%, so a shop with no supplies or fees reads "Parts {parts}% · Labor {labor}%".”
  • S10-R1: “Each KPI tile and the Sales by Customer tile shows a report link.”
